# The first round trip: what changed in v1.1.0

From v1.0.0 (2026-11-20, `b194bfc46`) to v1.1.0 (2026-11-20, this release), paragraph by paragraph.

0 paragraphs added, 0 removed, 3 changed in place, 36 unchanged. About 0 words added and 0 removed. Insertions are marked like this, deletions like this; unchanged runs are folded to one line; figures appear as their file names.

[all versions](../the-first-round-trip.md)

1 unchanged paragraph

Summary: Earlier today we had the first complete round trip of Sovereign WebWebsite with someone from outside. Kate Curtis-Evans, a founder I am collaborating with, understood the idea at once; I asked if she wanted a website, she said yes, and it was made during our call, in five designs, with a design agent that now runs on its own and on a schedule doing much better than design done inside the builder's session. Then the handover: Kate has a GitHub account, and the goal is that she edits her own site from her own Claude. It worked, and her Claude pushed its first change about 35 minutes after she accepted the invitation, but it was far harder than it should have been, and it took multiple rounds. Our earlier users were from the summit and already in the organisation; Kate was the first from outside, and getting her in meant making her a member of the organisation, a small piece of the over-privilege our platforms force on everyone. That is the lesson of always shipping: you only find where the friction is by doing it end to end. And it showed the next step: before anyone touches GitHub, a channel from the site itself to the agent, signed with a key the owner gets by QR code and sealed so only the agent can read it, the way VoiceDebrief already sent a message from an iPad to the conductor and got the answer back.

9 unchanged paragraphs, under In short {#in-short}, What happened {#what}

[Kate Curtis-Evans](https://kate-curtis-evans.founder.sovereignweb.site/) is a practising legal transcriber who built a live transcription platform, Audio Genius, without knowing how to code, and is now looking for a technical co-founder. She is a great founder, and I am collaborating with her. When I explained Sovereign Web,Website, she understood the value at once: a site that is hers, its files, its history and its address. I asked if she wanted one. She said yes, and we made it during our call.

8 unchanged paragraphs, under A design agent of its own {#design}, The handover {#handover}, The power of always shipping {#shipping}

Sovereign WebWebsite is only days old. It would have been easy to wait. But this is exactly why you ship as soon as something is a bit ready: our earlier users were from the summit and were already in the organisation, so none of this had shown up. Kate was the first from the outside world. People think these things just happen. They do not: doing it end to end is the only way to find where it should be easy and is not, and that is where the real product gets made. The start page has already been rewritten in the order that worked.
